chunks: Zurarah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Qasāmah was only instituted as a precaution for the people, so that if a wicked person wanted to kill a man or assassinate a man where no one could see him, he would fear that and refrain from killing.

key_terms.احْتِيَاطًا: As a precautionary measure to protect people and prevent harm.
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُ: A wicked or openly sinful person inclined toward wrongdoing.
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةُ: A legal procedure involving oaths in a murder case, used as an evidentiary safeguard.
key_terms.يَغْتَالَ: To kill someone stealthily or by assassination.

ai.seo_question: Why was qasāmah established in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that qasāmah was legislated as a protective legal measure for society. Its purpose is deterrence: a potential murderer, fearing the legal consequences, may refrain from killing in secret.
